one_month_reasoning: The one big event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings. The date is not confirmed; aggregators estimate Oct 22 [21]. Intel reported Q3 on Oct 23 2025 but on Oct 31 2024, so there is roughly a 15% chance the print lands after the Oct 31 close. Guidance is $15.8-16.8B revenue and $0.38 non-GAAP EPS [3]. Consensus already sits at $0.39 / $16.4B after 30 upward revisions in 30 days [2], so the bar has gone up. Intel's next-day reactions over the last 11 prints average about 11% in absolute size, and 8 of the 11 were negative. That includes -7.9% after the July 2026 beat-and-raise and +23.6% in April 2026 [18]. This sell-the-news habit, plus the stock's position after a +34% September at 58x FY27 EPS, offsets the short-term momentum base rate: across my semis sample, the median next-month return after a 35%+ month on top of a 100%+ year was about +5%, but survivorship bias pushes that number up [17]. Net effect: median about $119 (flat to slightly down) with a wide spread. I used a lognormal with a monthly sigma of 0.215, about the 76%/3.5 rule of thumb, since earnings vol is already part of realized vol. No index events, lock-ups or regulatory decisions are scheduled. The follow-on equity issuance (about $15B more planned [6]) could weigh on the stock if it is launched after earnings.

fair_value.method: Blend of a forward P/E (FY2028E EPS $2.70 x 35x = $94.50, weight 0.6) and EV/sales (FY2028E revenue $82B x 7x, less about $5B net debt, over 5.40B shares = $105, weight 0.4), giving about $99 as the value 12 months out. That is about 18% below the $120 price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028E EPS $2.70 x 35x NTM P/E (price in Oct-2027 set on FY2028 earnings)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $2.06 grown about 31%, close to the consensus FY26-to-FY27 growth (+36%, $1.52 to $2.06) with a little fade. Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 and the $0.38 Q3 guide [3] already annualize to about $1.60, which supports the trajectory.

Set above NVDA (28x) and TSMC's 10-year average (about 23x) [4] because Intel's EPS is growing off a depressed base and supply is constrained. It is well below today's 58-62x FY27 [4][1]. Intel's own history (P/S 1.5-12.5x over a decade [5]) shows peak multiples do not last, and the 2000 peak at about 50x EPS was followed by an 82% drawdown [19].

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: FY2028E revenue $82B x 7.0x EV/NTM sales = $574B EV; less ~$5B net debt; / 5.40B diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $72B FY27 consensus grown about 14%, slowing from consensus FY26-to-FY27 growth of about 14% ($63.1B to $72.0B) and Q2's +25% YoY [3].

Near the middle of Intel's decade P/S range of 1.5-12.5x [5] and below today's 11.7x EV/revenue [1]. Non-GAAP gross margin of about 42% [3] is far below NVDA/TSM levels, so a top-of-range multiple is hard to justify a year out.
Q2 debt of $50.5B less $29.7B cash gives $20.8B [3]. Subtract the $19.7B September raise [6], then add back roughly $4B of negative FCF from the capex ramp (Q2 adj. FCF was -$8.4B [3]).
5,104M Q2 diluted [3] plus 210.5M offering shares [6] gives about 5.31B (5.286B basic outstanding [1]). Add about 0.1B for SBC and part of the planned ~$15B follow-on issuance.

bear.story: The AI-CPU shortage eases or 18A/14A yields slip again (as the July 2026 reports flagged [9]) while capex and dilution rise. The multiple compresses toward 25x on about $2.40 EPS, a July-2026-style 40%+ drawdown that does not recover. My base-rate sample has about a 20% chance of a 30%+ loss after +150% years, and the 2000 analog is far worse [17][19]. Recession odds for 2027 of about a third (thin market) [11] add to the tail.

base.story: EPS keeps rising toward $2.70 FY28E, but the multiple de-rates from about 58x to 35-40x as growth normalizes and more shares are issued. The stock chops in the $85-140 range it has held since April and ends a little below today.

bull.story: Momentum continues, as it has for the median large-cap semi after a +150% year [17]. Intel lands external 14A foundry customers on top of the Google/Tesla deals [8], FY28 EPS heads past $3.50, and the market holds about 50x.

thesis_break_reason: $72 is below the July-2026 low ($81.79) and about 24% under the $95 September offering price [19][6]. At $72 the stock would trade at about 35x FY27 consensus EPS. Getting there would most likely require falling estimates (AI-CPU demand normalizing, 18A/14A yield or customer setbacks, margins stalling near 40%), not just multiple compression. July 2026 showed that ordinary de-rating on valuation worries takes the stock to the low $80s; a break below that, after a fresh $35B of equity, would signal a fundamental problem.

reasoning: Starting point: INTC is $120 after +258% in a year, +34% in September, and swings to $142 (June) and $82 (July). The stock sits at about 58x FY27 consensus EPS of $2.06, about 11x sales, and near the top of its decade P/S range [1][2][4][5]. Base rates: I pulled monthly history for 28 large semis and tech names [17] and found every month in which a stock was up 150% or more over the trailing 12 months. Taking the first such month per ticker-year (n=243), the median next-12-month return was +48%; 68% were up, 19% lost more than 30%, 12% lost more than 50%, and the log-return SD was 0.82. Restricting to 2002 onward and excluding the four mega-winners (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMD), n=72: median +25%, 71% up, log SD 0.63. These numbers carry heavy survivorship bias (the universe is today's winners; failures like 2000-era optical and memory names are missing), so I cut the momentum drift to about 0-10%. Valuation pulls the other way: my fair value of about $99 (35x FY28E EPS of $2.70; 7x FY28E sales) sits about 18% below the price, and Intel's own 2000 peak at about 50x was followed by -82% [19]. Sell-side consensus of $116 with 32 of 48 at Hold [1][10] agrees with a flat-to-down central case. Prediction markets: Manifold puts 41% on INTC touching $150 by end-2026 [15]. A driftless 76%-vol touch model gives about 55%, so play-money traders lean slightly bearish. Macro markets show little near-term recession or AI-bust risk in 2026 (8.5% / 8%) but rising 2027 tail odds (34.5% recession, 17.5% AI-bust by mid-2027, both thin) [11][13], plus no Fed cuts in 2026 [12]. Taiwan conflict odds of about 8.5% [14] are two-sided for Intel (it gains as a US fab, the market falls). Synthesis: a lognormal centered on $112, about 7% below spot, because overvaluation, about 4% dilution and the sell-the-news habit outweigh survivorship-adjusted momentum. I used sigma 0.66, between the base-rate sample's 0.63-0.82 and slightly below the 76% realized vol, since vol mean-reverts after spikes. This gives P(>=120) of about 46%, P(>=60) about 83%, and P(>=300) about 7%. Scenario mean (0.25x$60 + 0.5x$110 + 0.25x$185 = $116) is consistent. Research was limited: Twelve Data fundamentals were paywalled and Alpha Vantage hit its rate limit, so the price history came from Yahoo's public chart endpoint.
